There is no Free Market if:

  1. There is a monopoly on the creation of money. Interest rates (the price of money) cannot adjust when a single entity can increase or decrease the supply of money.

  2. There are various barriers to entry, including licensing fees that can cost thousands of dollars depending on the occupation. Other barriers can include business taxes, zoning laws, price floors, price ceilings, and barriers to interstate trade. A good example of a barrier is how the FDA forces new drugs to undergo extensive testing, even if the same drug has been sold without incident overseas for years.

  3. Governments subsidize certain industries or even specific sectors in an industry. Subsidies can be in the form of direct payments. An example is paying farmers when the sell their product at a lower than anticipated price. Subsidies can be in the form of a reduction in costs. One example is how California charges farmers only a fraction of what it charges residents for water. Subsidies and barriers to entry could be one an the same, similar to how there are import quotas on sugar, having sugar cost much more in the US than anywhere else, even though Caribbean sugar cane is nearby and plentiful. Public roads are another form of subsidies. Perhaps a new shopping center is being built on the edge of town, but there are no roads leading to the site. A local government may construct a road for the "public good".

  4. There is no free movement of people. If labor is not free to find higher wages, there is no freedom of association.

  5. There are laws that diminish the sanctity of private property. If a business is not free to discriminate, there is no freedom of association. If there is a ceiling to the liability that one entity has to pay to another entity for damages, one could perform very risky activities at a limited cost. One example is the BP oil spill, in which BP only had to pay for a fraction of damages.

  6. If people have to organize unions or fraternal societies in a limited framework set by the government, there is a limit to freedom of association.

Whether you advocate for or against the system of a free market is one argument. I am merely demonstrating that a free market does not exist in the United States.
